findings.reason: Verified: when dateOverrideExist is set and the slot is inside the override, line 134 returns true before the busy.every check at line 153, and busy reaches checkIfIsAvailable via ...schedule, so calendar bookings on override days are ignored.

Verified: workingHours.find returns truthy when any single same-weekday entry fails to contain the slot, and getWorkingHours (availability.ts:76-111) emits multiple entries per day for split hours and UTC-midnight overflow, so valid slots are dropped.
Verified the typo at line 142 (end uses slotStartTime), but buildSlots already filters slots that run past the range end (line 90), so the practical visible impact of this extra check is small.

Verified line 114 compares two freshly created Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, so the zero-length (start==end) override case is not caught and slots starting at that instant are returned as available.

The core defect is real (the day match uses the shifted UTC date and the * -1 sign flips the shift for negative-offset organizers), but the example is wrong: the code matches UTC Jan 4 rather than Jan 3, so the claimed Jan 2 evening slot removal does not happen as described.

The modulo-day wrap is real: buildSlots skips start>=end (line 68) while the working hours were already spliced out (lines 228-243), so the override can be silently dropped; however the stated numbers (1020/60) do not match the code's output for that example.

The Date.toString re-parse is a readability point with no effect on the instant, and the optional timeZone failure needs an unverified missing-timeZone input since getUserAvailability always supplies a timezone.

The test gap claims are accurate (no booking on the override day, single working-hours range per day), but this is a test gap on a path that the defects above would already expose, so it stays at a modest score.
